question: Put one pathogen genome in. What does each stage of the onset arm hand the next, does any stage cover less than the stage before it, and what changes when the reference changes?
answer: Six stages run, and the record carries the input and output of each, under both references. The surface stage is the one that used to cover less than its input: it had no caller, so the only surfaces ever measured were six named by hand, and SARS-CoV-2's RNA-directed RNA polymerase -- fifth of the ranked candidates -- was never asked about. It is exhaustive here, one row per chain, measured or refused with the reason. Folding now runs ahead of it and the residue ceiling is applied per fold unit rather than per chain, so a chain too long to fold whole is folded by its annotated functional regions instead and a chain no deposition covers can still be measured on predicted coordinates; the two are reported apart and neither is in the ranking, which is final at the end of stage 2. Stage 4 also reports the patch at the residues the curators marked as doing the chemistry, in this genome's own numbering, which is a different quantity from the largest patch on the chain and frequently somewhere else. One break remains and is recorded rather than drawn over: the library definition reads nothing the surface stage measured, so no later stage consumes stage 4's output.

limitations: The library stage reads nothing the four stages before it produced. The library definition is the same whatever the surface stage found, and the arrow a flowchart would draw there does not exist yet. The reorder sharpened this rather than fixing it: folding gained a consumer in the surface stage, and no later stage reads the surface stage, so stage 4 is the one stage here whose output nothing downstream consumes. `SURFACE_READ_BY` and `LIBRARY_READS_FROM_SURFACE` are both empty in the record for that reason. What stage 4 now produces for a reader rather than for a stage -- the marked residue positions, the residues within macrocycle reach of them and the patch measured there -- is the project lead's third ask and is not a substitute for that arrow.

Stage 2 now selects as well as scores. A chain is carried forward only where at least one of four evidence terms -- surface exposure, essential class, drugged class, structures in the family -- pays half a point or more, so a chain that pays nothing on all four is never folded, never measured and never searched for literature. Conservation is deliberately not one of the four: it says the genome was recognised, not that what was recognised is worth aiming at, and it is inherited unchanged by every chain cut from one polyprotein. The consequence is the one to hold against this record: a highly conserved protein whose relatives carry no localisation, no class keyword and no deposited structure leaves the pipeline at stage 2 on the strength of four annotations that are themselves a measure of how well studied it is. Every dropped row is named in the stage block with the four numbers it failed on.

Stages 3 and 4 measure and do not select. The rubric is five weights fixed before the run and no fold or surface term is among them, so the ranking is final at the end of stage 2 and the swap changed what can be measured, not what gets picked. Both stages record `changes_any_rank` false.

The residue ceiling now decides which fold UNITS reach the endpoint rather than which chains do. Nine of the twenty chains on the SARS-CoV-2 holdout are longer than it, including the three spike chains and the polymerase, and every one of them carries an annotated functional region at or under it, so the region is folded where the chain cannot be. The count, the names, the per-chain reason and the per-region outcome are in the record. Two things that follow and are not softened: a region folded on its own is a model of that region in isolation and has lost whatever its neighbours in the chain contributed to its shape, and a chain whose row carries no annotated range is never aligned, so it gets no region route even where its entry offers one -- the nucleoprotein is that case.

The gate in the surface stage is advisory: the patch spread across structures of one domain is comparable to the footprint it is thresholded against, so most rows that are not refused on localisation read borderline rather than yes or no.

The gate has a lower bound on patch area and no upper one, so a surface far larger than one footprint passes the area test although it is a region rather than a site. Nothing here turns on it, because every oversized patch in this record is refused on localisation first.

The folding stage locates a chain by aligning the relative's own residues against every ranked ORF, not by slicing this genome at the relative's coordinates. That is what makes the stage survive a holdout, and it is also a sequence-level correspondence and nothing more: a located window at 50 per cent coverage is this stage's claim that the chain is there, not a verified boundary.
One genome. The chain has been run on four pathogens and this record is one of them, chosen because it is the genome the project leads with.
interpretation: A record of what each stage produced. No binding, affinity, inhibition or antiviral property is predicted for any protein or any library member.
